statement: Find all functions $f : \mathbb{Q}_{>0} \to \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ such that $f(xy) \cdot \gcd\!\left(f(x)f(y),\, f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right)f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{y}\right)\right) = xy\, f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right)f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{y}\right)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$.

Let $n \geq 2$. Alice and Bob play on a country of $n$ islands, exactly two of which have a factory. Initially no bridges exist. They alternate building bridges (Alice first): a bridge may be built between islands $I_1$ and $I_2$ (not already connected by a bridge) only if at least one of them is connected to a factory. The player who builds a bridge connecting the two factories loses. Determine for each $n \geq 2$ who has a winning strategy.
In convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle B = \angle C$ and $\angle D = 90^\circ$. Suppose $|AB| = 2|CD|$. Prove that the angle bisector of $\angle ACB$ is perpendicular to $CD$.

A 	extit{Benelux $n$-square} ($n \geq 2$) is an $n 	imes n$ grid with $n^2$ pairwise distinct positive integers such that the GCDs of all rows and all columns yield $2n$ different values.

a) Prove that every Benelux $n$-square contains a cell with value at least $2n^2$.

b) A Benelux $n$-square is 	extit{minimal} if all $n^2$ numbers are at most $2n^2$. Determine all $n \geq 2$ for which a minimal Benelux $n$-square exists.
